questions.question: Rabindranath Tagore started Santiniketan institute in ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1901.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rabindranath Tagore started Santiniketan Institute in the year 1901.**
 
• Santiniketan was initially started as a school for children, later it became Visva-Bharati University, which is a central university located in Santiniketan, West Bengal.
 
• The main objective of Santiniketan was to combine the best of the East and the West and to create a place of learning that would be free from the constraints of the traditional education system.
 
• Rabindranath Tagore believed in the concept of **"Shantiniketan" or "abode of peace",** which was reflected in the name of the institution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Rabindranath Tagore:

 
• He was the youngest son of Debendranath Tagore, a leader of the Brahmo Samaj.
 
• He was the first Indian to win a Nobel prize for literature.
 
• He is also referred to as 'The Bard of Bengal'.
 
• He wrote the anthem of two countries - Jana Gana Mana, the Indian anthem, and Amar Sonar Bangla or My Golden Bengal, the Bangladesh anthem.

questions.question: Lomas Rishi cave is situated in which of the following Hills?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Barabar Hills.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Lomas Rishi cave is an ancient rock-cut cave located in the Barabar Hills of Bihar, India.**
 
• The cave is believed to have been built during the Mauryan Empire, around the 3rd century BCE.
 
• The Barabar Hills are known for their series of rock-cut caves, which were used as retreats for Jain and Buddhist monks.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

The Lomas Rishi Cave

 
• The Lomas Rishi Cave, also called the Grotto of Lomas Rishi, is one of the man-made Barabar Caves in the Barabar and Nagarjuni hills of Jehanabad district in the Indian state of Bihar.
 
• This rock-cut cave was carved out as a sanctuary.
 
• It was built during the Ashokan period of the Maurya Empire in the 3rd century BC, as part of the sacred architecture of the Ajivikas, an ancient religious and philosophical group of India that competed with Jainism and became extinct over time.
 
• Ajivikas were atheists and rejected the authority of the Vedas as well as Buddhist ideas.
 
• They were ascetic communities and meditated in the Barabar caves.
 
• Still, the Lomas Rishi cave lacks an explicit epigraphical dedication to the Ajivikas, contrary to most other Barabar Caves, and may rather have been built by Ashoka for the Buddhists.
 
• The hut-style facade at the entrance to the cave is the earliest survival of the ogee-shaped "chaitya arch" or chandrashala that was to be an important feature of Indian rock-cut architecture and sculptural decoration for centuries. 
 
• The interior surfaces of the chambers are very finely finished.

questions.question: Archana wishes to contest for Lok Sabha elections in India. What is the maximum limit of constituencies that can she contest?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Two.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Archana can contest from a maximum of two constituencies in the Lok Sabha elections in India as per the Representation of the People Act, 1951.**
 
• This limit was set to prevent candidates from having an unfair advantage by contesting from multiple constituencies simultaneously.
 
• The Lok Sabha is the lower house of the Indian Parliament, and its members are elected by the people of India.
 
• The Representation of the People Act, of 1951, is the law that governs the conduct of elections in India.
 
• The Act specifies the qualifications and disqualifications for candidates, the procedure for filing nominations, the conduct of elections, and the resolution of disputes related to elections.
 
• The Act also sets the maximum limit of two constituencies for candidates contesting in Lok Sabha elections to ensure fairness and prevent any undue advantage for candidates with multiple constituencies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Representation of the People Act, 1951:

 
 
• The Representation of the People Act, 1951 is an act of Parliament of India to provide for the conduct of the election of the Houses of Parliament and to the Legislature of each State. 
 
• It also includes its area of jurisdiction for:
 
 
• The qualifications and disqualifications for membership of the Houses. 
 
• Look over the corrupt practices.
 
• Other offenses in connection with such elections.
 
 
 
• Under the Representation of the People Act, 1951 the president’s decision is final.
 
• However, he should obtain the opinion of the election commission and act accordingly.

questions.question: Nahid Siddiqui was awarded Milapfest's Lifetime Achievement Award in October 2017. She is recognized for which dance form?

• ** Odissi **is a classical dance form from the eastern state of **Odisha.** It is characterized by fluid movements and sculpturesque poses.
 
• ** Sattriya** is a classical dance form from the northeastern state of **Assam**. It is known for its devotional themes and fluid, graceful movements.
 
• ** Kuchipudi **is a classical dance form from the southern state of **Andhra Pradesh**. It combines dance, music, and acting to tell stories from Hindu mythology.
 
• Hence, the statement is correct that Nahid Siddiqui was awarded Milapfest's Lifetime Achievement Award in October 2017 for her contribution to the Kathak dance form.

questions.question: What chemical element does "Mn" stand for in the science periodic table?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** **____**Manganese.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mn is the chemical symbol for the element Manganese.**
 
• Manganese is a transition metal that is commonly found in minerals such as **pyrolusite and rhodochrosite.**
 
• It is used in the production of steel and other alloys due to its ability to improve strength, hardness, and durability.
 
• Manganese is also important for biological processes in the body, including bone formation and metabolism.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Magnesium** is a chemical element with the symbol Mg and atomic number 12. It is a light, silvery-white metal that is commonly used in alloys, electronics, and as a dietary supplement.
 
• **Mendelevium** is a synthetic element with the symbol Md and atomic number 101. It was named after Dmitri Mendeleev, the creator of the periodic table.
 
• **Molybdenum** is a chemical element with the symbol Mo and atomic number 42. It is a refractory metal that is commonly used in alloys, electrical contacts, and as a catalyst.

questions.question: The moon moves around the earth in about ________ days.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __27 days__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] __Key Points__

 
• The moon orbits the Earth once every exactly 27.322 days. 
 
• It also takes approximately 27 days for the moon to rotate once on its axis.
 
• As a result, the moon does not seem to be spinning but appears to observers from Earth to be keeping almost perfectly still.
 
• Scientists call this synchronous rotation.
 
• The side of the moon that perpetually faces Earth is known as the near side.
 
• The opposite of the "back" side is the far side. Sometimes the far side is called the dark side of the moon, but this is inaccurate.
 
• When the moon is between the Earth and the sun, during one of the moon phases called the new moon, the backside of the moon is bathed in daylight.
 
• The orbit and the rotation aren't perfectly matched, however.
 
• The moon travels around the Earth in an elliptical orbit, a slightly stretched-out circle.
 
• When the moon is closest to Earth, its rotation is slower than its journey through space, allowing observers to see an additional 8 degrees on the eastern side.
 
• When the moon is farthest, the rotation is faster, so an additional 8 degrees are visible on the western side.
 
• [IMAGE: https://earthsky.org/upl/2017/07/moon.orbit_-e1498934371864.jpg]

questions.question: Which of the following articles of the Indian constitution provides for National commission for Scheduled Castes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Article 338**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** The correct answer is option 4, i.e. Article 338 of the Indian Constitution provides for the National Commission for Scheduled Castes.**
 
• This article was inserted by the** 65th Amendment Act of 1990.**
 
• The National Commission for Scheduled Castes is a constitutional body that is responsible for safeguarding the rights and interests of the scheduled castes and monitoring the implementation of constitutional safeguards for them.
 
• The Commission investigates and monitors all matters relating to the constitutional and other legal safeguards for the protection of the rights and interests of the scheduled castes and submits reports to the President and the Parliament.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Article 337**: This article deals with the appointment of a special officer for linguistic minorities.
 
• **Article 344**: This article deals with the appointment of a Commission to examine the conditions of backward classes.
 
• ** Article 343: **This article deals with the official language of the Union.

questions.question: The historical Sher-Shah Suri Marg runs between ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Sher-Shah Suri Marg runs between** __Delhi and Amritsar. __**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sher-Shah Suri Marg is a historical road that was built during the reign of Sher Shah Suri in the 16th century.**
 
• It was built to connect the Mughal Empire's capital Delhi with the province of Punjab. The road was later extended to the Afghan border during the British era.
 
• The road is also known as the Grand Trunk Road and is one of the oldest and longest roads in South Asia. It covers a distance of over 2,500 km and passes through several major cities like Delhi, Amritsar, Lahore, and Kolkata.
 
• The road played a significant role in the trade and commerce of the Mughal Empire and later the British Raj. It was also an important route for the movement of troops during wars and conflicts.
 
• The road has undergone several renovations and upgrades over the years, but it still retains its historical significance and attracts tourists from all over the world.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Sher Shah Suri Marg

 
 
• National Highway No.1 is known as Sher Shah Suri Marg
 
• It connects Delhi To Amritsar via Ambala and Jalandhar
 
• Previously it was known as Grand Trunk Road (GT Road)
 
• It was built by Sher Shah Suri in the 16th century
 
 
 
• Sher Shah Suri
 
 
• Founder of the Suri Dynasty in India
 
• Grand Trunk Road (GT Road)
 
• The oldest and longest road in Asia
 
• It runs roughly 2400km from Teknaf, Bangladesh to Kabul, Afghanistan.

questions.question: Which of the following profession is a type of seasonal unemployment?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Farmer.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Seasonal unemployment takes place when people are unemployed during a particular season or time of the year when labour demand is lesser than usual. **The agriculture sector suffers from it because of the seasonal nature of crops and farming seasons. **
 
• Disguised unemployment occurs when more people are employed than actually required. The marginal productivity of labour is zero. In agriculture more people work in the field, the same amount of work can be finished with a smaller workforce. 
 
• Frictional unemployment occurs when a person is unemployed by his choice and he is seeking a better job opportunity, it is good for the economy as the worker is looking for a job where he can be more productive. It is not found in the agriculture sector. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Other unemployments are-

 
• Structural Unemployment 

 
 
• It refers to a situation that arises due to the change in the structure of an economy. For Example- when a labour-intensive economy turns into a capital-intensive economy.
 
 
 
• Cyclical Unemployment-
 
 
• Occurs due to deficiency ineffective demands from consumers which leads to a fall in production and low demand for labour.

questions.question: Limestone is a type of ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Sedimentary rock__.

__
 
• Limestone is a type of sedimentary rock.
 
• It is a type of carbonate sedimentary rock.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] Key Points__

__
 
• Mineral calcite and aragonite from limestone.
 
• Mineral calcite and aragonite are different crystal forms of calcium carbonate.
 
• When these minerals precipitate out of water containing dissolved calcium, then limestone is formed.
 
• Biological and non-biological processes both are involved in the formation of limestone.
 
• Fossils are contained by limestone.
 
• So information about ancient environments and the evolution of life can be obtained from limestone.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/292e0c96dd6c006ce1f3ef21b86308c7c73a2bc69f508d641b46f352d114f429.png] Important Points__

 
• The sedimentary rock contains 20-25% carbonate rocks and 75% part of the rock is limestone.
 
• Dolomite is contained in the carbonate rock.
 
• In the shallow marine environment, most of the limestone is formed.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an example of "viviparous" animals?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bird.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Viviparous animals are those that give birth to live young instead of laying eggs**.
 
• Birds are** not viviparous as they lay eggs and the young hatch from them.**
 
• Dogs, cats, and cows are all examples of viviparous animals as they give birth to live young.
 
• Viviparity has evolved in **many different animal groups, including mammals, reptiles, and some fish.**
 
• The opposite of viviparity is oviparity, where animals lay eggs that hatch outside of the body.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Birds are oviparous animals, meaning they lay eggs instead of giving birth to live young.
 
• Dogs, cats, and cows are all mammals, which are characterized by their viviparous reproductive strategy.
 
• Reptiles are also known for their diverse reproductive strategies, with some species being oviparous, some being viviparous, and others being ovoviviparous (where eggs are retained inside the body until hatching).
 
• Fish also exhibit a wide range of reproductive strategies, with some species being oviparous, some being viviparous, and others using external fertilization.

questions.question: The transformation of the larva into an adult through drastic change is called ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**metamorphosis.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Metamorphosis is the process of transformation from a larva or nymph into an adult organism.**
 
• This process involves significant changes in morphology, physiology, and behavior, and is typically accompanied by the breakdown and reorganization of tissues and organs.
 
• Metamorphosis is a common feature of many animal groups, including insects, amphibians, and some fish, and is critical for their survival and reproduction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Budding: **It is a form of asexual reproduction in which a new individual develops from an outgrowth or bud on the surface of the parent organism. This process is observed in organisms such as yeast, hydra, and some types of plants.
 
• **Shifting:** This term is not related to any specific biological process, and its meaning can vary depending on the context.
 
• **Bulging:** This term can refer to the expansion or protrusion of a body part or structure, such as the bulging of the eyes in some medical conditions. It is not related to the process of metamorphosis.

questions.question: The Ahom Kingdom in India was located in the ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Brahmaputra Valley.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Ahom Kingdom was located in the Brahmaputra valley, which is in the northeastern region of India.**
 
• The kingdom was established in **1228 and lasted until 1826 when it was annexed by the British East India Company.**
 
• The Ahom rulers were known for their** military prowess and their resistance against the Mughal Empire.**
 
• The kingdom was also known for its architecture, literature, and culture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Chota Nagpur plateau** is located in eastern India and is known for its mineral resources.**
 
• Vindhayas is a mountain range in central India that stretches from **Gujarat to Madhya Pradesh.**

questions.question: The Directive Principles of State Policy is included in which part of the Indian constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Part IV.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Part IV of the Indian Constitution deals with the Directive Principles of our State Policy (DPSP).

 
 
• They are an 'instrument of instructions' which are enumerated in the Government of India Act, 1935.
 
 
 
• Articles 36 to 51 are included in this section.
 
• The provisions contained in this Part cannot be enforced by any court.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Part II of the Constitution** deals with citizenship and includes provisions on who is considered a citizen of India, how citizenship can be acquired or lost, and the rights and privileges of citizens.
 
• **Part III of the Constitution **outlines fundamental rights, which are enforceable by law. These rights include the right to equality, freedom of speech and expression, freedom of religion, and the right to constitutional remedies.
 
• **Part I of the Constitution **contains provisions on the Union and its territory, citizenship, and fundamental rights. It also includes provisions on the Constitution's preamble, which outlines the objectives and principles of the Constitution.

questions.question: Indore gharana is one of the vocal gharanas of Indian classical music. It was founded by ________.

• Ustad Bundu Khan was a renowned sarangi player from the Punjab Gharana. He is not associated with the Indore Gharana.

questions.question: Diwali marks the day when lord Ram returned to Ayodhya after ________ years of exile after defeating king ravan.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** option 4, which is 14 years of exile.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Lord Ram went into exile with his wife Sita and brother Lakshman, as per the command of his father King Dasharatha.
 
• **He spent 14 years in the forest, facing numerous challenges and fighting demons.**
 
• After completing the exile, Lord Ram returned to Ayodhya and was welcomed with great joy and celebration by the citizens of Ayodhya. This day is celebrated as Diwali, also known as the festival of lights.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Ramayana** is about Rama, a prince of Kosala, who was sent into exile.
 
• His wife Sita was abducted by the king of Lanka, Ravana, and Rama had to fight a battle to get her back.
 
• He won and returned to Ayodhya, the capital of Kosala, after his victory.
 
• Like the Mahabharata, this was an old story that was now written down.
 
• **Valmiki is recognized as the author of the Sanskrit Ramayana**.
 
• Ramayana consists of **24,000 shlokas and seven cantos (kaṇḍas)**.
 
 
• The epic Ramayana, dated variously from the **5th century BCE to the first century BCE.**
 
 
 
• Valmiki was a Sanskrit poet and celebrated as **Adi Kavi**.
 
• There are **several versions** (many of which are performed) of the Mahabharata and the Ramayana, popular amongst people in different parts of the subcontinent.

questions.question: As per the 2011 census of India, which Indian state has the lowest sex ratio?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Haryana.__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to the 2011 Census, Haryana has the lowest child sex ratio (834 per thousand men), while Arunachal Pradesh has the highest (972) among the Indian states.
 
• The ratio of females to men in the 0–6 age group is known as the child sex ratio.
 
• India's child sex ratio was 927 in the census of 2001 but dropped to 919 in the census of 2011. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• Sex Ratio in India:

 
 
• Sex ratio is used to describe the number of females per 1000 of males.
 
• Sex ratio is a valuable source for finding the population of women in India and what is the ratio of women to that of men in India.
 
• In the Population Census of 2011, it was revealed that the population ratio in India 2011 is 943 females per 1000 males.
 
• The Sex Ratio 2011 shows an upward trend from the census 2001 data.
 
• Census 2001 revealed that there were 933 females to that of 1000 males.
 
• For decades India has seen a decrease in the sex ratio 2011, but since the last two of the decades, there has been a slight increase in the sex ratio.
 
• Since the last five decades, the sex ratio has been moving from around 930 females to that of 1000 males.
 
 
 
• Sex Ratio of few Indian States:
 
 
• Kerela - 1084
 
• Puducherry - 1037
 
• Tamil Nadu - 996
 
• Andhra Pradesh - 993
 
• Delhi - 868
 
• Chandigarh - 818
 
• Dadra and Nagar Haveli - 774
 
• Daman and Diu - 618
